 Commercial LPG Price Rises Again, Hitting Hotels and Restaurants
 By Ayesha Siddiqui 
 November 2, 2026 
 0 
 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp 
 Commercial LPG Price Rises Again, Hitting Hotels and Restaurants 
 Commercial LPG prices rose by Rs 10 for a 19-kg cylinder while aviation turbine fuel (ATF) increased by Rs 1.37 per litre in the latest monthly revision by oil marketing companies, raising operating costs for urban hotels, restaurants and airlines. The price changes were reported as being in line with elevated international benchmarks.
 In Delhi, a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder will now cost Rs 2,820. The cylinder will be priced at Rs 2,775 in Mumbai, Rs 2,971 in Kolkata and Rs 2,994.50 in Chennai, according to the report. Commercial LPG is widely used by hotels, restaurants and other businesses that depend on regular cooking-fuel supplies.
 The latest increase is the third consecutive monthly rise in commercial LPG prices. The repeated revisions add to the input costs of food-service businesses, although the supplied report does not specify whether individual establishments will pass the increase on to customers.
 ATF prices have risen to Rs 138.5 per litre after the latest increase. This is the fourth straight monthly hike in aviation turbine fuel rates, according to the report. ATF is a significant operating input for airlines, and its price is revised alongside LPG at the beginning of each month.
 The changes have not affected the 14.2-kg domestic LPG cylinder, whose price remains Rs 942 in Delhi. Petrol and diesel prices also remain unchanged. The distinction between commercial and domestic cylinders means the latest LPG increase is focused on business users rather than household consumers using the smaller cylinder.
 Oil marketing companies revise ATF and LPG prices on the first day of every month, using international benchmark prices and the rupee-dollar exchange rate as reference points. The latest adjustment comes after crude oil prices remained elevated through October. Brent crude was trading at $113.43 per barrel on Saturday, while the Indian basket of crude oil averaged $119.96 per barrel in October, described in the report as a record.
 The different rates across cities reflect variations in state tax structures. For urban businesses, the immediate impact will therefore depend on both the national benchmark-linked revision and the local price applicable in each state. The next monthly revision will determine whether commercial LPG and ATF prices continue to move higher or change direction.
